Description:
Two cones that share a common INSCRIBED SPHERE. By the theorem of Monge, two surfaces of revolution of
second order circumscribing the same sphere intersect in TWO PLANE CONICS, and those two conics cross
at the two points where both surfaces touch the sphere at the same place - and there the two cones are
tangent to each other and to the sphere. So this is an inner tangential contact with a NODE of the
intersection curve, at two points at once.

The common sphere has radius 10 and sits at the origin, never built - it only fixes the geometry:
  coneWide  half angle 45 deg, axis +z, apex (0, 0, 14.1421356237) = 10/sin 45, opening downwards,
            height 30, base radius 30
  coneNarrow half angle 30 deg, axis (0, sin 45, cos 45), apex 20*axis = (0, 14.1421356237, 14.1421356237),
            opening back towards the origin, height 45, base radius 45*tan 30 = 25.9807621135
A cone of half angle alpha whose apex is at distance d from the centre touches the sphere of radius rho
when rho = d*sin alpha, which is what both apex distances 10/sin 45 and 10/sin 30 = 20 are for.
Both touch the sphere along a circle, and the two circles cross at
  (7.0710678119, 0, 7.0710678119) and (-7.0710678119, 0, 7.0710678119)
which are therefore the two tangential contact points of the cones (residual on both mantles < 1e-14).

The two half angles are DIFFERENT on purpose. With equal half angles the two contact points are mirror
images in the plane of the two axes and can never lie in the seam plane. With 45 and 30 degrees they can,
and here they do: both axes lie in the yz plane, and the contacts come out at y = 0, exactly on the two
seam edges of coneWide, which - being a cone about the z axis through the origin - is split into its two
half mantles precisely in the xz plane. Contact, node and face boundary again coincide.
See ConeCylinderCommonInsphere for the same construction placed in the interior of the faces.
Expected:
Exact operand volumes: coneWide pi/3*30^2*30 = 9000*pi = 28274.3338823081,
coneNarrow pi/3*(45*tan30)^2*45 = pi/3*675*45 = 10125*pi = 31808.6256178783.
The contacts are properly inside both mantles: at axial distance 10 of 30 from the apex of coneWide and
15 of 45 from the apex of coneNarrow, so neither an apex nor a base plane takes part in the degeneracy.

There is no closed form for the intersection, so it was integrated by Monte Carlo over the box
60x60x31, 4e6 samples:
  intersect       15123 +- 19
  union           44960 +- 19    ( = 28274.334 + 31808.626 - intersect )
  wide - narrow   13151 +- 19
  narrow - wide   16686 +- 19
The identity union + intersect = 28274.3338823081 + 31808.6256178783 = 60082.9595001864 is exact and is
the sharpest check, together with difference = operand - intersect for both ways round.

Both cones are convex, so intersect must be a single convex solid - never several parts, never empty -
and all four results must be closed and consistent.
Status:
OK since 2026-08-28. FIXED on 2026-08-28 by the second repair of the same day (Shell.cs, Surface.cs and the new
SurfaceContacts.cs). Two things changed at once and both were needed:
the geometry became RIGHT where it was wrong, and the face partition became REPRODUCIBLE - the case is
stable over 4 runs now, so it finally carries a baseline. Before that it could not be pinned at all:
a face on a periodic surface was split in one run and left whole in the next, and a regenerate run
refused to record anything. The volume never moved even then, which is why the geometry could be
judged while the partition still wandered.

WHAT WAS WRONG, and how the repair shows in the numbers. The intersection used to be 84 mm3 too big -
15223.55 measured by inspect.properties at precision 1e-5 against a true 15139.4 - and its extent gave
the reason away: it reached z = 14.1421356237, the APEX of coneWide, although that apex lies outside
coneNarrow and the true intersection stops at z = 11.1535. A region around the apex of the wide cone
was taken into the intersection although it belongs to the difference.
Now:
  insphereInter  volume 15139.3924347, and its extent ends at z = 11.1464 instead of 14.1421
  insphereWideMinusNarrow comes out as THREE solids instead of two, and the new third one is
  83.2227237821 with its extent reaching exactly z = 14.1421356237 - the piece around the apex, back
  where it belongs, and its volume is the 84 mm3 that were missing. That is the clearest possible
  confirmation that this was the defect and that it is gone.

The independent values: deterministic quadrature 15137.72 / 15138.82 / 15139.18 on 800, 1600 and 2400
intervals (converging to about 15139.4), Monte Carlo 15144 +- 11 over four seeds. The recorded 15139.39
agrees with both to better than 1e-4, where the old result was off by 5.5e-3.

THE 83 mm3 PIECE, INVESTIGATED 2026-08-28. This is the one object of the case that keeps it from being
green in a full suite run: insphereWideMinusNarrow#2 is recorded as 83.2227237821 when the case runs
alone and comes out as 83.6939595286 when it runs inside the suite (area 204.52 against 202.81). The
investigation says the BREP IS RIGHT AND DETERMINISTIC and the recorded number is a measurement.

1. The true volume is 84.1259. The piece contains the apex of coneWide, and coneWide is convex, so the
   piece is star shaped as seen from that apex and its volume is an integral over the directions,
   V = 1/3 * integral of rmax(omega)^3 dOmega, where rmax is the smaller of the distance to the base
   plane and the distance to the entry into coneNarrow - both from a quadratic. Simpson over the 45
   degree cap of directions converges cleanly:
     200x400   84.128842
     400x800   84.126662
     800x1600  84.126117
     1600x3200 84.125981      -> 84.12594
   An independent voxel flood fill from the apex (h = 0.20 / 0.12 / 0.08: 83.888 / 83.948 / 83.956,
   rising, and voxel counting underestimates) confirms the same body and the same magnitude.

2. ShapeIt agrees, when asked precisely enough. inspect.properties at precision 1e-5 gives
   84.12580837 - 1.6e-6 from the computed value - and repeating the whole construction three times in
   one session gives 84.1258097435 every time, with bounding boxes identical to the last digit. So the
   boolean produces the same body every time and that body is correct.

3. The recorded value is a triangulation. ShellMetrics measures volume and area at
   PrecisionFor(shell) = size * 1e-3 (BRepSummary.cs), and at that precision this body - a sharp cone
   tip - measures 1.07 or 0.51 percent low. Which of the two you get depends on what was triangulated
   BEFORE, because Face.AssureTriangles (Face.cs, line 7159) reuses an existing mesh:
     if (trianglePoint != null && precision >= trianglePrecision / 2.0) return;
   so a request is served by any mesh that is at most twice as coarse. Minimal reproduction, one
   session, the same body built twice:
     fresh solid, asked at 1e-3 straight away          83.2227237821
     fresh solid, asked at 1.5e-3 first, then at 1e-3  83.6939595286
     either of them, asked at 1e-5                     84.1258097435
   Same BRep, same requested precision, two different volumes - the request history decides.

WHAT THAT MEANS FOR THE CORPUS. The comment on ShellMetrics.PrecisionFor was written against exactly
this failure ("a case really did come out with a 10% different area depending on whether it ran alone
or in a full suite") and it closed the precision == 0.0 path, but not this one: passing a deterministic
precision does not guarantee a deterministic mesh. Two things follow, and they are separate:
  REPRODUCIBILITY  a measurement meant for a baseline has to force its own triangulation instead of
                   accepting one that happens to exist.
  ACCURACY         1e-3 relative is too coarse for a body with a tip: 1 percent error here, and the
                   same reason the operand cones in ConesTangentAtMantlePoint measure 0.9 percent low.
                   1e-5 costs more but lands on 1.6e-6.
Until that is decided the case stays as it is: it passes alone and fails in a full run, on this one
field. Widening RelativeTolerance would hide it, but 0.6 percent on a volume is more than the 0.55
percent error this very case uncovered in the boolean, so that is not the right trade.
